labeler: blind independent review, generic OWASP rubric, no knowledge of the tool under test

labels.note: The /evaluate route passes the untrusted request.form['expression'] (set at line 376) straight into eval() -- direct Python code injection / remote code execution from an unauthenticated POST.

The /cookie route calls pickle.loads(b64decode(request.cookies['value'])) on an attacker-controlled cookie -- deserialisation of untrusted data yields arbitrary code execution (a crafted pickle runs on load).
The /lookup route concatenates request.form['address'] (line 357) into a shell string and runs it via rp()->popen() (rp defined line 172), so 'x; <cmd>' gives OS command injection.

The /sayhi route interpolates request.form['name'] (line 454) into a template string that is then passed to render_template_string() -- server-side template injection in Jinja2, exploitable to RCE (e.g. {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}).

The /listservices route builds a WHERE clause by string-formatting the user-controlled 'category' query param (request.args at line 476) directly into SQL, then executes it at line 484 -- classic SQL injection via a string-formatted query.

The /xml route parses untrusted request.form['xml'] with an lxml XMLParser explicitly configured load_dtd=True and no_network=False (line 397) -- XML External Entity (XXE) injection enabling local file disclosure and SSRF.

verify_token() honours the 'None' JWT algorithm (allowed at line 32; verify_token_none at 242-263 accepts a token whose signature segment is empty), so an attacker can forge an unsigned token with sub='admin' and reach the admin branch at line 520 -- JWT signature-verification bypass / privilege escalation.

notes: Provenance: stephenbradshaw/breakableflask, a real public single-file intentionally-vulnerable Flask app (recall case; NOT authored by us). Vulnerability classes are corroborated by the repo's own README.md and vulnerability_index.md (Python code injection, OS command injection, pickle deserialisation, XXE, padding oracle, SSTI, SQL injection, JWT None/alg-confusion). Labeled independently from reading main.py. This case deliberately tests a Python (Flask) surface the tool may not cover -- labeled honestly regardless. Deliberate non-findings: the AES KEY and ADMIN_SECRET are random per-run (lines 24/26), not hardcoded secrets; app.run binds 127.0.0.1 by default (line 661), so no exposed-bind label. A padding-oracle exists in /config (decrypt at line 431) and reflected HTML injection/XSS is pervasive across routes; these were not separately labeled to keep the high-confidence RCE/injection set clean.
